# Contributing to CEP

Thank you for helping build CEP. Contributions from people with different skills and viewpoints are welcome.

## Ways to contribute

- Research and source-checking
- Writing, editing and translation
- Software engineering, testing and security review
- UX, accessibility and visual design
- Governance, legal and human-rights analysis
- Mission design and evaluation

## Before starting

1. Read the [Founding Charter](../FOUNDING-CHARTER.md) and [Governance proposal](../GOVERNANCE.md).
2. Search existing issues and pull requests.
3. For substantial work, open an issue first to agree on scope.
4. Do not begin work that could expose people to risk without an explicit safety review.

## Pull requests

- For anything that changes the interface, follow the
  [agent UX checklist](../docs/ux/AGENT-UX-CHECKLIST.md): the fa/en × light/dark ×
  390/1440 matrix, the audit scripts, and the before/after rating.
- Use a fork and branch; do not expect direct write access.
- Keep each pull request focused and explain the problem it solves.
- Link related issues and include tests or evidence where relevant.
- Cite sources for factual, legal, scientific or historical claims.
- Label assumptions, uncertainty and contested interpretations.
- Explain privacy, security, accessibility and misuse implications.
- Do not include credentials, personal data, private correspondence or identifying details of vulnerable people.
- Be respectful when responding to review and be willing to revise or withdraw work.

## AI-assisted contributions

AI agents are welcome to help with research, drafting, translation, code and tests. They must:
- disclose meaningful AI assistance in the pull request;
- never invent sources, quotations, identities, test results or community support;
- provide reproducible steps and identify uncertainty;
- avoid submitting large volumes of low-quality or duplicative changes;
- never request or use secrets, credentials or private participant data;
- follow the same review and conduct rules as all contributors.

AI agents do not receive votes, maintainer status or authority to represent people.

## Review and merging

A pull request is a proposal, not an entitlement to merge. A human maintainer decides whether it is accepted and records the required review; agents cannot approve their own work or bypass branch protections, checks, or community review. After an authorized human maintainer has approved the specific pull request and all applicable requirements pass, an agent may execute the merge only when explicitly instructed by that maintainer. If authority or required gates are unclear, stop and ask. High-impact changes to the charter, governance, safety policy or mission scope require the additional community review process described in GOVERNANCE.md. A merged document is not automatically community-ratified.

## Conduct

Be curious, accurate, patient and respectful. Criticise ideas without attacking people. See [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) and [Security Policy](SECURITY.md).
